item.subject: science
item.stem:
The diagram shows sunlight reaching a concave mirror. Parallel rays meet at one place on a scrap of paper.

Why does a bright hot spot form on the paper?

options.A: The concave mirror reflects the parallel rays so that they meet at one small point, concentrating the light energy there.
options.B: The concave mirror spreads the parallel rays evenly across the paper, so the whole paper warms at once.
options.C: Any mirror makes a hot spot on the paper; the concave shape does not matter.
options.D: The paper heats first, and that heat then bends the rays toward the bright spot.
